```{r opts, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

Pay the setup once, not per figure. One text file describes your experiment. Every gene
thereafter is a few clicks or lines of R from a clean, fair figure, great for exploring your data.
Sharing is simple then too.

# Install

PlotTrellis needs R 4.5 or later, on Linux or macOS. Installing from scratch (dependencies included) takes ~45
minutes:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("BiocManager")
install.packages("PlotTrellis",
                 repos = c("https://aleks-wehi.r-universe.dev",
                           BiocManager::repositories()))
# mouse gene names (for human data: "org.Hs.eg.db")
BiocManager::install("org.Mm.eg.db", update = FALSE)
```

# A project from a colleague

Open it with the path of their `samples.txt` (you need read access to their data):

```{r colleague, eval=FALSE}
library(PlotTrellis)
run_plottrellis(project_dir = "tcell-project",
                samples_txt = "/data/smithlab/tcell_2026/samples.txt")
```

# Your first figure

Start R, ensuring you're in a folder you can write to.

```{r app-example, eval=FALSE}
library(PlotTrellis)
run_plottrellis(project_dir = "PlotTrellis-example", # full or relative
                samples_txt = pt_example())
```

This creates `PlotTrellis-example` folder in your working directory and opens the bundled example in the app: mouse mammary basal cells (Basal) and luminal
progenitors (LP) at five genes, with RNA-seq, splice junctions, transcript expression, ATAC,
H3K36me3 and Hi-C. `project_dir` is the folder PlotTrellis keeps the project in.

Write *Eya2* in the gene box, pick the samples, add tracks and click **Generate figure**. 

Or in R:

```{r code-example, eval=FALSE}
proj <- pt_project(project_dir = "PlotTrellis-example",
                   samples_txt = pt_example())
fig  <- pt_figure(proj, "Eya2", tracks = c(
  "transcript_expression", "junctions", "ATAC", "H3K36me3",
  "transcripts_annotated", "genes"))
pt_save(fig, "Eya2.pdf")   # or .svg, .png
```

Both give this figure:

```{r example-figure, echo=FALSE, fig.alt="Eya2 in mouse mammary basal cells and luminal progenitors: transcript expression, splice junctions, ATAC and H3K36me3 coverage for each, then the annotated transcripts and the gene."}
library(PlotTrellis)
proj <- pt_project(project_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "PlotTrellis-example"), samples_txt = pt_example())
pt_figure(proj, "Eya2", tracks = c("transcript_expression", "junctions", "ATAC", "H3K36me3", "transcripts_annotated", "genes"))
```

Then try *Lrrfip1*, *Acot7*, *Dzip1* or *Cxcl14*. Close
the app's tab to stop it. Rerunning with just the `project_dir` reopens it. A human example (GM12878 and K562 cells around *PSME2*) can be opened with
`samples_txt = pt_example("human")` and a new `project_dir`.

# Your own data

A project is one file, `samples.txt`: your genome, then one row per sample and one column per
kind of data. Three ways to make it, easiest first:

1. **In the app.** Run `run_plottrellis(project_dir = "my-project")`. A wizard asks for your
   genome, data folder and samples, and saves the project. Can take time for large projects.
2. **With an AI assistant.** Paste [our prompt](samples-txt-ai-prompt.html) into a chat AI
   (ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot). It asks about your files and gives you the file and the command
   that opens it.
3. **Yourself.** The format is [here](samples-txt.html).

PlotTrellis can intake the following processed files (incorrect ones are raised, try if unsure):

| Data | Files |
|---|---|
| Coverage | bigWig, bw |
| Transcript expression | `quant.sf`: a table of transcript IDs and TPMs (Salmon output) |
| Splice junctions, loops | BED12, BED6, STAR `SJ.out.tab`, BEDPE, HiCCUPS |
| Hi-C | `.hic`, `.cool`, `.mcool` |
| Peaks, regions | BED, narrowPeak, broadPeak |

It also needs a GENCODE or Ensembl GTF for mouse or human. Further details: [Input data](inputs.html).

# Share it

Send a colleague the path to your `samples.txt` (a wizard project's is `project_samples.txt`
in its `project_dir`). Use full paths for `data_root` and `gtf_path` so they can read your data irrespective of where the `.txt` is.

NB: They need read permissions to the data and GTF.

# Troubleshooting

Everything a project keeps is in its `project_dir`. Close the app first. To start fresh, keep a
copy of your `samples.txt` outside the `project_dir` (a wizard-made project keeps it inside, as
`project_samples.txt`), delete the `project_dir`, and recreate the project as above.

<style>
.code-box { position: relative; margin: 1.2em 150px 1.2em 0; }
@media screen and (max-width: 991px) { .code-box { margin-right: 0; } }
.code-box pre { margin: 0; padding-top: 12px; padding-bottom: 12px; }
.copy-code { position: absolute; top: 4px; right: 4px; font-size: 12px; opacity: 0; }
.code-box:hover .copy-code, .copy-code:focus { opacity: 1; }
</style>
<script>
if (navigator.clipboard) document.querySelectorAll("pre").forEach(function (pre) {
  var button = document.createElement("button");
  button.className = "copy-code";
  button.textContent = "Copy";
  var code = pre.querySelector("code") || pre;
  var box = document.createElement("div");
  box.className = "code-box";
  pre.parentNode.insertBefore(box, pre);
  box.appendChild(pre);
  button.onclick = function () {
    navigator.clipboard.writeText(code.innerText).then(function () {
      button.textContent = "Copied";
      setTimeout(function () { button.textContent = "Copy"; }, 1500);
    });
  };
  box.appendChild(button);
});
</script>
